dedupe_keys.name: abides agent based interactive discrete event market simulator

description: ABIDES (Agent-Based Interactive Discrete Event Simulation) is an environment built from the ground up to support research on AI agents in market applications, described in an arXiv paper of 26 April 2019. It simulates tens of thousands of trading agents interacting with an exchange agent, supports configurable pairwise network latencies between agents and the exchange, and uses a message-based design modelled on NASDAQ's published ITCH and OUCH equity trading protocols. The paper illustrates configuration with sample code, validates the environment with example trading scenarios and applies it to a market impact model, and proposes uses such as developing machine-learning trading algorithms. The code is published in an original repository and in J.P. Morgan Chase's public repository; neither could be opened from this session, so access terms, licence and language were not read. Coverage is generic markets, not tied to a country. Caveats: it models exchange trading, not payment or settlement systems, and calibration to real markets is left to users. For simulation it runs agent-based scenarios of trading disruptions, latency and market stress in financial market infrastructure. Related catalogue records include BoF-PSS2 and the OFR Financial Stress Index.
